messages.subject: Referencing y-axis limits inside a grid panel when scale=free
parts:
Here's another question from my 2-dataset plot.  I want to modify the plot below so that it prints a line segment (or thin bar) down from the top to, say, 1/4 of the y axis.  The y axis is free, and is a function of multiple variables in the "cewall" data set.  From the all.fronts data set I don't know what values to use for the y axis, so in the example below I just picked an arbitrary data point. Is there any way to access the current y-axis scale?

ggplot () +
geom_segment(data = all.fronts, aes(x = doy, xend=doy, y=200, yend=Inf))  +
geom_line(data = cewall, aes(x = doy, y = avgmoths, color=variable)) +
geom_errorbar (data = cewall,aes(x = doy,ymin = (avgmoths - stderr),
     ymax = (avgmoths + stderr), color=variable), width = 0.1)  +
facet_grid (year~., scales = "free_y")

Data are below.

Thanks,
Jennifer

messages.subject: Re: Referencing y-axis limits inside a grid panel when scale=free
parts:
On Mon, Nov 9, 2015 at 8:41 AM, Jennifer Krauel <unquench...@gmail.com> wrote:
ggplot () +
geom_segment(data = all.fronts, aes(x = doy, xend=doy, y=200, yend=Inf))  +
geom_line(data = cewall, aes(x = doy, y = avgmoths, color=variable)) +
geom_errorbar (data = cewall,aes(x = doy,ymin = (avgmoths - stderr),
     ymax = (avgmoths + stderr), color=variable), width = 0.1)  +
facet_grid (year~., scales = "free_y")

Jennifer, 

Your cewall data.frame doesn't have a stderr in it so the code is not reproducible any more, so I've taken that part out. 

Essentially, it's better to precompute what you're asking for and then merge that variable with the all.fronts data.frame. 

require(dplyr)
require(ggplot2)

all.fronts <- structure(list(date = structure(c(14855, 14878, 14884, 14893,
14902, 15221, 15236, 15239, 15247, 15256, 15259, 15264, 15270,
15274, 15280, 15286, 15294), class = "Date"), doy = c(247L, 270L,
276L, 285L, 294L, 248L, 263L, 266L, 274L, 283L, 286L, 291L, 297L,
301L, 307L, 313L, 321L), year = structure(c(1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L,
2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L), .Label = c("2010",
"2011"), class = "factor")), .Names = c("date", "doy", "year"
), row.names = c(NA, -17L), class = "data.frame")

all.fronts <- 
cewall %>%          # start with cewall
group_by(year) %>%  # group by year
summarise(quartermoths= 0.75 * max(avgmoths, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%  # compute 75% of the maximum moths  
full_join(all.fronts, .)  # join this data back to all.fronts so you can use it in ggplot

ggplot () +
geom_segment(data = all.fronts, aes(x = doy, xend=doy, y=quartermoths, yend=Inf))  +
geom_line(data = cewall, aes(x = doy, y = avgmoths, color=variable)) +
facet_grid (year~., scales = "free_y")

ggplot () +
geom_segment(data = all.fronts, aes(x = doy, xend=doy, y=quartermoths, yend=Inf))  +
geom_line(data = cewall, aes(x = doy, y = avgmoths, color=variable)) +
facet_grid (year~., scales = "free_y")
